title: Average, Mixture & Alligation
intro: Average is total divided by count — but SSC rarely asks it that plainly. It dresses it up as a changed average when a person joins or leaves, an innings score, or an average speed for a two-leg journey. Alligation is the partner idea: a fast visual rule for the ratio in which two ingredients (or two prices, or two speeds) must mix to hit a target average. Learn the cross rule and weighted-average problems become ten-second cross-multiplications.

items.name: Average
items.formula: sum of values / number of values

topics.name: Average Basics
topics.details: Average = sum / count, so sum = average x count. When one value changes, the total changes by the same amount, and the average shifts by (change / count). The 'replacement' pattern — a person of weight A leaves and one of weight B joins, changing the average by d for n people — gives B - A = n x d. Always think in totals, not averages, when something is added or removed.

solved.problem: Average of 5 numbers is 18. Their sum?
Average of 10 numbers is 25; one number 30 is removed. New average?
A batsman's average in 16 innings is 36. To raise it to 38 in the 17th, what must he score?
solved.solution: Old total 576; new total 38 x 17 = 646; required = 70.

solved.problem: The average weight of 8 people rises by 2.5 kg when a 56 kg person is replaced by a new one. New person weight?
solved.solution: Increase in total = 8 x 2.5 = 20; new = 56 + 20 = 76 kg.

topics.name: Weighted Average
topics.details: When groups of different sizes combine, the overall average is the weighted average: (n1 a1 + n2 a2) / (n1 + n2). This is the engine behind average marks of two sections, average price of mixed stock, and average speed when times differ. Do not average the averages unless the group sizes are equal.

solved.problem: Section A (40 students) averages 60; section B (60 students) averages 70. Combined average?
20 kg of rice at 30/kg mixed with 30 kg at 40/kg. Average price?
A man drives 2 hours at 40 km/h and 3 hours at 60 km/h. Average speed?
solved.solution: Distance = 80 + 180 = 260 km; time 5 h; avg = 52 km/h.

solved.problem: Two classes: 25 students avg 16 years and 15 students avg 20 years. Combined average age?

topics.name: Alligation Rule
topics.details: Alligation gives the ratio in which two things at known values mix to hit a mean value: cheaper : dearer = (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper). Picture the cross: write the two values at the top corners, the mean in the middle, and take diagonal differences. It works for prices, concentrations, speeds and even average ages — any weighted average run backwards to find the mix ratio.

solved.problem: In what ratio mix rice at 24/kg and 40/kg to get 30/kg?
How much water to add to 40 L of milk to make the average value drop from 20 to 16 per litre (water value 0)?
solved.solution: milk:water = (16-0):(20-16) = 16:4 = 4:1; for 40 L milk, water = 10 L.

topics.name: Mixtures & Replacement
topics.details: When a fraction of a mixture is repeatedly removed and replaced with one ingredient (the classic 'milk-and-water, remove r litres and top up with water' problem), the remaining original ingredient after n operations is initial x (1 - r/V)^n, where V is the total volume. This geometric decay is the SSC favourite for liquid replacement.

solved.problem: A 40 L cask of milk: 8 L removed and replaced with water, once. Milk left?
Same cask, the operation done twice. Milk left?
A vessel has 50 L milk; 10 L drawn and replaced by water twice. Milk:water now?
20% of wine is drawn and replaced with water, repeated. After how many steps is wine below 50%?
solved.solution: Each step x 0.8: after 1 -> 80%, 2 -> 64%, 3 -> 51.2%, 4 -> 40.96%. So after 4 operations.

shortcuts: Think in totals when a value is added/removed: change in total = n x change in average.
Average speed for equal distances = 2ab/(a+b) (harmonic mean), NOT (a+b)/2.
Repeated replacement: remaining = initial x (1 - r/V)^n.
mistakes: Averaging two averages without weighting by group size.
Using (a+b)/2 for average speed when distances (not times) are equal.
Flipping the alligation diagonals (cheaper goes with the dearer-difference).
Forgetting the replacement decay is multiplicative, not subtractive.
pyq: SSC mixes changed-average (innings, replacement), weighted average (two sections/mix prices) and alligation for alloy/milk problems. Liquid replace-and-top-up is a recurring Tier-2 item.

flashcards.q: Average speed, equal distances a, b?

summary: Work averages through totals; weight by group size; use the alligation cross to find mix ratios; and apply (1 - r/V)^n for repeated liquid replacement. Average-speed for equal distances is the harmonic mean 2ab/(a+b).
